title: An arrow from Rama's bow
hookLine: the Sundara Kanda opens with Hanuman pressing a mountain until water runs from the rock, then going as Rama's arrow, not his own
carry: dasya: going as God's arrow, not your own
tomorrow: The trees that saw him off

lines: THE BOOK MANY FAMILIES READ WHOLE.
cards: Of the seven books of the Ramayana, this is the one many Hindu families read on its own, start to finish, sometimes over days, sometimes when life is hard. It's the Sundara Kanda, the beautiful book.
And it begins mid-breath. The first verse opens, tato rāvaṇanītāyāḥ sītāyāḥ śatrukarśanaḥ: then, the tamer of enemies, of Sita, carried off by Ravana.
It goes on: he set out to find her trail, along the path the sky-travelers use. No warm-up. Just: then.

teach.b: Hanuman stands on Mahendra, and Valmiki slows everything down. Hanuman presses his hands and feet into the mountain.
The rock gives. Streams burst out of it. Animals bolt from their caves, and sages and celestial beings rise into the air to get out of the way.
A whole mountain shakes because one being is gathering himself. Then Hanuman says what he'll do.

teach.h: LIKE AN ARROW FROM RAMA'S BOW.
teach.b: He'll go to Lanka like an arrow loosed from Rama's bow. If Sita isn't there, he'll search heaven. Then he crouches, draws in his breath, and springs.
Notice the comparison he chooses. Not a bird, not the wind, though he's the wind's son. An arrow from Rama's bow: he isn't going for himself; he's the shot Rama is firing across the sea.
This is why Hindus hold Hanuman up as the great example of dasya, devotion as a servant, one of the nine ways of bhakti the Bhagavata lists. And the servant here isn't small.
He's the strongest being in the story, and he points all of it at someone else's purpose. Krishna says it in the Gita too: whatever you do, offer it to me.
So many Hindus, before work, a test or a meal, quietly offer it to God, and some say after: Krishnarpanam, given to Krishna.
Why is the book called beautiful? Valmiki never says, and people give different answers. One many tell: it's where hope returns.
The story was stuck on a beach. Now it moves.

how: Many Hindus recite the Sundara Kanda in full at home or in temples, often over several days, and some families read it in times of difficulty or before a new undertaking; Hanuman is the classic picture of dasya, devotion as service.

s: the Sundara Kanda opens with a long introduction
its first word is 'then', and it goes straight to Hanuman on the mountain.
water bursts from the rock when Hanuman presses Mahendra
animals flee and sages rise into the air.
dasya, devotion as a servant, means being weak or small
Hanuman is the strongest one in the story, and he points all of it at Rama's purpose.

games.q: Nani tells you to go into your test 'as Ram's arrow.' by today's story, what does she mean?
o: do your best and offer it to God: the effort is yours, the glory isn't.
God's will is all that matters, so you don't need to study.
games.why: Hanuman goes as Rama's arrow: all his strength, pointed at Rama's purpose. that's dasya, devotion as service, and it never skips the effort.

practice: Before your next task, fold your hands for one breath and offer it: many Hindus say Shri Ramarpanam, or Krishnarpanam, given to God.
Then plant your feet, as Hanuman pressed the mountain, and breathe slowly, attention pointed one way. If you'd rather not pray, name who or what the work is for, beyond you, and offer it there.

wordCard.voice: The leap. Hanuman pressing Mount Mahendra until water runs from the rock, calling himself an arrow from Rama's bow, and springing out over the sea.

orig.note: Sanskrit sundara, beautiful: the name of the fifth book, the Sundara Kanda.
